title: A social media API for AI agents: from upload to verified delivery
description: How to connect an agent to Gruvi, upload finished media, choose exact account targets and check whether a post actually published.
author: Gruvi
takeaways: Separate media preparation, scheduling and published delivery.
Choose connected account IDs instead of guessing a destination.
Use the HTTP API directly or the local MCP connector.

sections.title: What a social media API should do for your agent
paragraphs: An agent can prepare a caption and choose a publishing time, but it still needs an authenticated way to send that work to the right social account. Gruvi provides that distribution layer through a hosted HTTPS API and a local MCP server.

The workflow starts with content you already have. Upload a finished video, attach a thumbnail, select connected destinations and publish now or schedule ahead. You can perform the same work manually in the dashboard. Gruvi does not need to generate the media to distribute it.

Keep the boundaries visible in your own application. An uploaded video is library media. A scheduled post is a future instruction. A published result is a platform outcome. Treating those as separate records makes it easier to explain progress and recover from failures.

sections.title: Start with a named agent key
paragraphs: Create an account, verify your email and connect your social channels in the workspace. Create a named agent key for the workflow you are building. Store it in an environment variable or secret manager and send it as a bearer token to the Gruvi API.

Call the account and connected-accounts endpoints before sending anything. The account response supplies your userId. Each connected destination has its own accountId, even when two accounts use the same platform. Agent keys authorize your Gruvi account; they are not the platform OAuth tokens, and they cannot mint more agent keys.

sections.title: Upload media once, then reuse its ID
paragraphs: Request a signed video upload URL, upload the file to storage and finalize it in Gruvi. The file upload and the API call use different credentials: send your bearer key only to Gruvi, never to the signed storage URL. The videoId returned by finalization identifies the library item you can reuse for later posts.

Prepare a title, caption and any custom thumbnail before scheduling. Do not assume that a stored thumbnail will become the native cover on every platform. The platform settings guide explains the delivery options and restrictions for each destination.

sections.title: Schedule with exact targets and a future time
paragraphs: Send the selected account IDs with the platform identifiers returned by Gruvi. X uses the identifier twitter. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp with a timezone for scheduling, and choose a future time. Give the operation a stable requestId so an uncertain response can be retried without inventing a second logical schedule.

Free setup lets you connect channels, prepare media and configure your agent. Submitting a post requires an active publishing plan, trial or complimentary access. If a plan is needed, your agent can return a Stripe-hosted checkout link for the account owner to complete.

sections.title: Read the result before calling the job finished
paragraphs: Read the schedule record and the destination delivery results after the scheduled time. An accepted queue request does not establish that a public post exists. TikTok creator-inbox delivery produces a draft for review, which is different from a live post.

For a network timeout during an immediate send, inspect the existing delivery state first. Automatically resubmitting the same video can create duplicate public posts. Record the operation ID, destination account and current platform state in your agent workflow so you can report what actually happened.

title: Bulk video scheduling: plan a batch without duplicating posts
description: Schedule up to 20 finished videos through the Gruvi dashboard, API or MCP connector, with individual times and retry-safe results.
author: Gruvi
takeaways: A batch contains 1 to 20 existing videos, each with its own time and caption.
A multi-status response can contain both accepted and rejected items.
Retry an unchanged batch with the original requestId.

sections.title: Build the batch from finished videos
paragraphs: Bulk video scheduling is useful when the media is ready and the work is mostly repetitive: select the same channels, assign publishing times and check several results. In Gruvi, a bulk request contains 1 to 20 posts. Each item references a video in your account and has its own title, caption, future time and connected-account targets.

Upload the videos before you submit the batch. In the dashboard, open Bulk Scheduling, upload several files or choose existing library items, then select destinations. Set the first publishing time and an interval to fill the schedule, and review the time for every row before submitting.
Spacing posts is a planning convenience, not a guarantee of better reach. Choose the cadence that fits your audience and the material you have, rather than filling every available slot.

sections.title: Send a stable batch request
paragraphs: Use POST /api/gruvi/scheduled-posts/bulk with one stable requestId. Preserve both that ID and the order of the posts when retrying an uncertain response. Changing the content, order or timing represents a different batch and should use a new ID.

The example below shows the shape of a batch item. Replace the example IDs and timestamp with your own media, account and future publishing time. Add another object to posts for each video you want to schedule.

sections.title: Read every item in a partial result
paragraphs: A 201 response means all items were scheduled. A 207 response contains per-item results, so the batch may be partly accepted. Inspect the success value, scheduleId and any error for each index. Do not label the entire batch successful because one item received a schedule ID.

Gruvi validates the media and destination ownership before creating the schedules. Scheduling allowances are consumed atomically, which prevents simultaneous requests from exceeding the account limit. A valid batch can still have partial results when the remaining monthly allowance cannot cover every item.

sections.title: Keep retries and cancellations deliberate
paragraphs: If the response is uncertain, check the calendar and retry the unchanged batch with the same requestId. Accepted items retain their schedule IDs and do not consume a second allowance. To change a caption or time, inspect the existing schedule first instead of submitting a slightly different batch under its old identity.

A future schedule that has not started can be cancelled. Gruvi refunds that scheduled allowance once. A post that is already publishing or finished cannot be made safe to resend just by cancelling a calendar entry.

sections.title: Use the same batch from an MCP agent
paragraphs: The MCP tool gruvi_bulk_schedule_videos accepts the same logical batch. Your agent should keep the batch request ID in its task state, inspect per-item results and report any rejected rows. It should also distinguish scheduled acceptance from published delivery.

TikTok videos in the bulk dashboard use creator-inbox review. Other networks attempt publication at the scheduled time, subject to their permissions and media requirements. Keep that distinction in your campaign checklist so a review draft is not mistaken for a public post.

artwork.alt: Gruvi arranging video tickets across calendar sheets with several tentacles, viewed from above.

title: Instagram and TikTok carousels: upload, order and schedule your images
description: Prepare 2 to 10 images as a Gruvi carousel, choose Instagram or TikTok and understand the difference between a saved set, a draft and a published post.
author: Gruvi
takeaways: A carousel is an ordered image post, not a batch of separate video posts.
Gruvi accepts 2 to 10 JPEG, PNG or WebP images, up to 5 MB each.
Choose one exact Instagram or TikTok destination per carousel operation.

sections.title: What is a carousel post?
paragraphs: A carousel combines several images into one post that a viewer can move through. It works well for a short visual sequence, a product walkthrough or a set of ideas that need more than one frame. It is a different workflow from bulk scheduling, where each video becomes a separate scheduled post.

Gruvi supports image carousels for Instagram and TikTok. You bring the images, arrange their order and add the caption. The same preparation flow is available in the dashboard and through the API or MCP connector. Platform account eligibility and permissions still apply.

sections.title: Prepare a consistent image set
paragraphs: Choose 2 to 10 JPEG, PNG or WebP files, each no larger than 5 MB. Gruvi validates the uploaded image bytes and places each image on a 1080 by 1350 canvas. Images are fitted without cropping, so a different aspect ratio can leave padding around the original artwork.

Review the first image as an introduction and the last image as the end of the sequence. Keep text readable in the final canvas, and check the image order before saving. The preparation step creates a reusable carousel in your account; it does not publish it.
In the dashboard, open Carousel Posts to select files, move an image earlier in the order and save the set. You can prepare the images before choosing a publishing plan.

sections.title: Use the API upload sequence
paragraphs: Request a signed upload URL for each image with its file type and byte size. Upload the file directly to that URL with the matching Content-Type. Keep the returned imageKey in display order, then call POST /api/gruvi/carousels with the title, caption and ordered imageKeys.

The image keys must belong to the authenticated account and come from the carousel upload flow. Arbitrary external image URLs are not accepted. Your Gruvi bearer key belongs on the API requests, not on the signed storage PUT.

sections.title: Publish now or choose a future time
paragraphs: Select one exact connected account on Instagram or TikTok. An immediate publication includes platform, accountId and a stable requestId. To schedule instead, send the saved carousel ID, one destination and a future scheduledTime to its schedule endpoint.

If you want to send the same images to a second destination, create a separate operation with that account and its own request ID. This keeps delivery results and retries unambiguous for each network.

sections.title: Check whether it is live or waiting for review
paragraphs: TikTok defaults to creator-inbox review, so a successful send can produce a draft that you must finish inside TikTok. Do not report that draft as a live post. Direct publishing also depends on the account and application permissions available for that platform.

After an uncertain immediate send, read the carousel publication using the same requestId before retrying. The MCP tools gruvi_upload_carousel, gruvi_publish_carousel, gruvi_schedule_carousel and gruvi_get_carousel_publication cover those same stages.

title: A practical guide to social media analytics across five platforms
description: Understand Gruvi analytics for TikTok and YouTube, engagement summaries for Instagram, Facebook and X, and how to handle missing metrics.
author: Gruvi
takeaways: Compare metrics only when their definitions and coverage match.
TikTok and YouTube have summary and trend endpoints.
Instagram, Facebook and X expose recent-post engagement summaries in beta.

sections.title: Start by checking what each endpoint measures
paragraphs: A social media analytics API is most useful when it is clear about the data it returns. A view, an impression, a reaction and a share are different measurements. Different platforms can also return different time ranges, post types and permission-dependent fields.

Gruvi has analytics pages for TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook and X. TikTok and YouTube have summary and trend endpoints. Instagram and Facebook add permission-dependent account insights for seven or 28 complete days, alongside recent-post lifetime counts. X has beta recent-post summaries. These measurements have different time ranges and should stay separate in reports.

Choose an exact connected accountId when requesting metrics. That matters if you operate several channels on one platform: an account-wide label such as Instagram is not enough to identify which brand or creator account you meant.

sections.title: TikTok and YouTube: summaries and trends
paragraphs: The existing TikTok integration reads published-video metrics, including views, likes, comments and shares when the platform grants access. The YouTube integration also provides summary and trend views. Use those endpoints when you need the measurements exposed by the connected channel.

Read the response and its time or grouping fields before charting the result. Grouping a published video by its creation date is different from measuring the engagement it received during a particular day. Avoid labelling every trend series as daily impressions unless the returned data actually means that.

sections.title: Instagram, Facebook and X: recent engagement
paragraphs: The beta engagement summaries read up to 25 recent posts and cache the result for five minutes. Instagram returns available likes and comments. Facebook returns available reactions, comments and shares. X uses the platform identifier twitter and reads the public metrics permitted by the connected account and API access.

The response identifies its coverage as recent_posts. Totals refer to that returned sample, not the account's lifetime activity. A follower value is returned where the integration has it; fields the platform does not provide remain unavailable.
The same summary can feed a dashboard card or an agent report. Include the account, update time and post count next to the numbers so the reader knows which data they are comparing.

sections.title: Treat unavailable data differently from zero
paragraphs: A null metric means the value is unavailable. Zero is an actual measurement. Substituting zero for a missing field makes a report look complete while changing its meaning. In a human dashboard, show Unavailable. In an agent report, preserve null and explain the coverage.

A 403 response may indicate missing read permissions, a platform role issue or API access that needs attention. Reconnect the correct account and inspect the platform requirements. Repeating the same request rapidly will not grant a permission that the account does not have.

sections.title: Separate publishing health from content performance
paragraphs: First confirm that the post was delivered to the intended account. Then inspect its performance. A low engagement count cannot explain a failed upload, and a successful queue response cannot establish that a post went live.

For a scheduled workflow, keep the schedule ID and delivery state alongside the analytics account ID. Your agent can report a delivery failure immediately and produce an engagement summary later, once the platform makes those measurements available.

artwork.alt: Gruvi examining a heart and rising engagement chart through a magnifying glass.

title: Connect Claude Code or Codex to your social publishing workflow
description: Install Gruvi's local MCP server, store your key safely and verify account access before asking an agent to upload or schedule content.
author: Gruvi
takeaways: Local stdio MCP clients and direct HTTP workflows have different setup paths.
Verify the account and connected destinations before the first send.

sections.title: Choose MCP or the HTTP API
paragraphs: MCP lets a compatible agent client discover named tools and their input schemas. Gruvi's local MCP server exposes tools for uploading media, scheduling posts, preparing carousels, inspecting delivery and reading analytics. It calls the hosted Gruvi API on behalf of your account.

Use the HTTP API directly when your automation already makes authenticated web requests. OpenClaw and other automation workflows can use that contract without pretending to be a local MCP client. A browser-based client that requires hosted remote MCP transport cannot use a local stdio configuration as a remote endpoint.

sections.title: Create a key for this workflow
paragraphs: Set up the Gruvi account, verify the email and connect the channels you want to use. Create a named key in Agent Access. Use separate keys for separate agents or workflows so you can revoke a single integration without replacing every client configuration.

Store the key in your client's secret configuration or an environment variable. Do not put a real key in a public repository, screenshot or chat. The server determines the account from the key, so you should not derive a userId by splitting the key string.

sections.title: Install the pinned package and configure your client
paragraphs: Gruvi's published package is @agent-gruvi/gruvi-mcp-server. The documented setup pins version 2.1.0, which exposes 26 tools and two readable documentation resources. It requires Node.js 20 or newer.

Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Codex can launch a local stdio server, but their configuration file formats differ. Use the exact client-specific example in the setup guide. Pass GRUVI_API_KEY through the environment and leave the API URL at its documented production value unless you are intentionally using a different environment.

sections.title: Check the connection before any publication
paragraphs: Reload the MCP client, list the available tools and call gruvi_get_user_info. Then call gruvi_get_social_accounts and confirm the selected account names and IDs. These are read-only checks and do not require sending a real test post.

The server also exposes gruvi://docs/quickstart and gruvi://docs/api resources. An agent can read those instructions to understand authentication, publishing access, safe retries and platform delivery differences before it acts.

sections.title: Give the agent a specific publishing task
paragraphs: A useful request identifies the finished media, destination accounts, caption and time. Ask the agent to inspect existing media and schedules first so it can reuse a video instead of uploading it again. Keep changes to the media itself separate from distribution instructions.

For batches, use gruvi_bulk_schedule_videos and preserve the batch request ID. For image sequences, use the carousel tools. After sending, ask for the schedule or publication ID and the actual destination state. A public URL is useful evidence only when the platform has returned a real post URL.

Setup and media preparation are available before subscribing. When publishing access is needed, the agent can retrieve plans and return a hosted checkout link. The account owner completes that checkout; generating the link does not activate the subscription.

artwork.alt: Gruvi connecting a cable between code brackets and a video play symbol.

title: How to retry a social publishing request without creating duplicates
description: Use stable request IDs, inspect delivery after uncertainty and distinguish a scheduled post, a TikTok draft and a confirmed publication.
author: Gruvi
takeaways: A timeout means the response is uncertain, not that nothing happened.
Use stable request IDs where the endpoint supports them.
Inspect existing delivery before retrying an immediate video publication.

sections.title: A lost response is not a failed post
paragraphs: A publishing request can reach a server even when the client does not receive its response. If an agent treats every timeout as permission to send again, it can create duplicate posts or duplicate calendar entries. The first step after uncertainty is to inspect the existing state.

Keep the video or carousel ID, selected destination IDs, logical request ID and any returned schedule ID in your workflow state. That small record is more useful than a success message that omits which account was targeted or what the platform actually returned.

sections.title: Give a logical operation a stable identity
paragraphs: Gruvi scheduling, bulk scheduling and carousel publication support a stable requestId. Reuse the original ID with the original payload after an uncertain response. Do not generate a fresh ID each time the network client retries.

A new caption, different destination or reordered batch is a different request. Reusing an old ID with changed content is rejected so that one identity cannot silently describe two publishing operations. For a batch, preserve the post order as well as the individual content and times.

sections.title: Immediate video publishing needs a delivery check
paragraphs: Do not assume every endpoint has the same idempotency behavior. Before repeating an immediate video publication, read that video's per-platform social-upload status. The existing batch-social-upload path should not be blindly resubmitted just because its HTTP response was lost.

Inspect the result for each selected destination. A multi-platform request can succeed for one network and fail for another. Keep the successful result, diagnose the failed destination and avoid resetting the whole aggregate operation while another platform is still processing.

sections.title: Use the right words for the current state
paragraphs: Scheduled means that a future instruction was accepted. Processing means work is still in flight. Published means the integration has confirmed the platform outcome. TikTok creator-inbox delivery is a draft awaiting review, even when its transfer completed successfully.

Do not substitute a profile URL for a missing post URL. A link to a channel proves that the channel exists, not that the requested video or image set was published. Report the operation ID and current status when the platform has not provided a native post link.

sections.title: Respect rate limits and access failures
paragraphs: A 429 response includes retry guidance. Honor Retry-After rather than launching parallel retries. Gruvi shares request allowances across an account's keys, so switching keys does not create a fresh account budget.

A 403 response can indicate a publishing-plan, verification, ownership or platform-permission requirement. Fix the specific access problem before sending again. A 503 protection failure is also not permission to bypass the protected endpoint.

Your agent's final report should name each intended destination and say published, scheduled, draft, processing or failed. Include the exact next step for unresolved work. Clear state reporting is part of the publishing workflow, not an optional summary at the end.

artwork.alt: Gruvi holding duplicate posts in a retry loop while guiding one post toward a check mark.
